1	// SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause
2	// Copyright (c) 2025-2026 Kevin Barnard and minix.rs Contributors
3	//! The user-space virtual-address map the kernel and user space agree on.
4	//!
5	//! Everything else in this crate describes a *message* ABI — bytes on the wire
6	//! between two processes. This module describes an *address* ABI: the kernel
7	//! installs a mapping at one of these VAs and a user-space process dereferences
8	//! it, with no message in between. Slice 5.3's TTY driver is the first consumer:
9	//! the kernel pre-maps the PL011 MMIO page at [`TTY_UART_VA`] with Device
10	//! attributes while building TTY's address space, and TTY's `pl011.rs` does
11	//! volatile loads and stores there.
12	//!
13	//! That is why this is not in [`crate::message`]: nothing here is a payload
14	//! offset or a pointer predicate, and getting a value wrong is a data abort in
15	//! user space, not a rejected message.
16	//!
17	//! ## The device window
18	//!
19	//! [`USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_BASE`] carves one whole L1 slot (1 GiB of VA space,
20	//! costing exactly one L1 + L2 + L3 frame for the pages actually mapped) out of
21	//! the user VA range, well clear of every VA any process occupies today:
22	//!
23	//! | VA | What |
24	//! |---|---|
25	//! | `0x0010_0000` | server / init / worker ELF images (`user.ld` base) |
26	//! | `0x0020_0000` | server stack page (`SERVER_STACK_VA`) |
27	//! | `0x0040_0000` / `0x0080_0000` | demo stub code / stack pages |
28	//! | `0x0100_0000` | VM's heap origin (`region::HEAP_BASE`) |
29	//! | `0x0200_0000` | VM's anonymous-mmap arena (`region::MMAP_BASE`) |
30	//! | `0x4000_0000` | **the device window** |
31	//! | `0x8000_0000` | [the ramdisk window](RAMDISK_WINDOW_BASE) (slice 5.7) |
32	//!
33	//! Two of those entries *grow* on request — VM's heap (`brk` raises its end) and
34	//! VM's mmap arena (a bump cursor that never reuses addresses) — so
35	//! `servers/vm/src/region.rs` bounds **both** at [`USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_BASE`] with a
36	//! runtime `REGION_LIMIT` check rather than relying on the 992 MiB of slack. A
37	//! compile-time assert on their *bases* is not enough: it proves only where each
38	//! region starts.
39	//!
40	//! Phase 6's virtio-mmio drivers get further pages of the same window; the
41	//! 16 MiB size is sized for that rather than for TTY's single page.
42	//!
43	//! ## The ramdisk window
44	//!
45	//! [`RAMDISK_WINDOW_BASE`] is the second kernel-owned window, and it is placed
46	//! *above* the device window on purpose: `REGION_LIMIT` in
47	//! `servers/vm/src/region.rs` is the base of the **lowest** kernel-owned window,
48	//! so every window added above that low-water mark needs no VM edit at all. The
49	//! `USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_BASE + USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_SIZE <= RAMDISK_WINDOW_BASE`
50	//! assert below is what keeps that ordering true, and it is what makes the
51	//! ramdisk's separation from every *process* VA transitive through the device
52	//! window's.
53	//!
54	//! Unlike the device window this one maps **ordinary RAM**, not MMIO: the kernel
55	//! copies the boot archive's `rootfs` blob into freshly allocated frames and maps
56	//! them `Prot::RW_DATA`. So none of the `prot.device` machinery is involved —
57	//! these frames take the normal `free_frame` path in every leaf sweep. RW rather
58	//! than RO because slice 5.10's write path is then a body change in the driver
59	//! rather than a re-mapping in the kernel.
60	//!
61	//! These constants are deliberately **not** emitted into the generated C headers:
62	//! no Phase 5 C touches them (musl's `write()` goes to VFS, not to a driver's
63	//! MMIO window or ramdisk), and a header constant is an ABI promise that would be
64	//! awkward to retract once Phase 6 reshapes the windows.
65	
66	use crate::message::{USER_PAGE_SIZE, USER_VA_TOP};
67	
68	/// Base of the user-space device (MMIO) window. One whole L1 slot at 1 GiB.
69	pub const USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_BASE: u64 = 0x4000_0000;
70	
71	/// Size of the user-space device window: 16 MiB, i.e. 4096 pages. TTY uses one;
72	/// the rest is headroom for Phase 6's virtio-mmio register pages.
73	pub const USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_SIZE: u64 = 0x0100_0000;
74	
75	/// VA at which the kernel pre-maps the PL011 UART's MMIO page into the TTY
76	/// driver's address space (slice 5.3, decision D1). Page 0 of the window.
77	///
78	/// The mapping is installed once, at boot, by
79	/// `arch::aarch64::userland::load_boot_server` — TTY is a boot server with no
80	/// way to ask for it (there is no `VMCTL_MAP_PHYS`; D1 deferred VM-mediated
81	/// device mapping to Phase 6), so this is a bring-up step exactly like the
82	/// server stack page.
83	pub const TTY_UART_VA: u64 = USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_BASE;
84	
85	/// Base of the user-space ramdisk window. One whole L1 slot at 2 GiB (slice 5.7).
86	///
87	/// Kernel-owned like the device window, and deliberately *above* it so
88	/// `region::REGION_LIMIT` — the base of the lowest kernel-owned window — does not
89	/// move when a window is added.
90	pub const RAMDISK_WINDOW_BASE: u64 = 0x8000_0000;
91	
92	/// Size of the ramdisk window: 4 MiB, i.e. 1024 pages.
93	///
94	/// Sized from the format rather than from today's image: seven direct zones plus
95	/// one single-indirect block address `7 + 1024` zones at a 4 KiB block size,
96	/// which is 4.03 MiB — so a window this size can hold any image MinixFS can
97	/// address without a double-indirect reader (see `fs/mfs`'s `read` module).
98	pub const RAMDISK_WINDOW_SIZE: u64 = 0x0040_0000;
99	
100	/// VA at which the kernel maps the boot ramdisk into the `memory` driver's
101	/// address space (slice 5.7, decision D3). Page 0 of the window.
102	///
103	/// Installed once, at boot, by `arch::aarch64::userland::load_boot_server` — the
104	/// `memory` driver is a boot server with no way to ask for it — and reported to
105	/// that driver alone via `SYS_GETINFO(GET_RAMDISK)`.
106	pub const RAMDISK_VA: u64 = RAMDISK_WINDOW_BASE;
107	
108	/// Size of one L1 slot in the 4 KiB-granule, 4-level, 48-bit-VA walk this
109	/// kernel uses: 512 L2 entries × 512 L3 entries × 4 KiB = 1 GiB.
110	const L1_SLOT_SIZE: u64 = 1 << 30;
111	
112	// The window must start on an L1-slot boundary and fit inside one slot, so the
113	// whole device window costs a single L1 entry and can never share an L2 subtree
114	// with an ordinary mapping.
115	const _: () = assert!(USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_BASE.is_multiple_of(L1_SLOT_SIZE));
116	const _: () = assert!(USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_SIZE <= L1_SLOT_SIZE);
117	const _: () = assert!(USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_SIZE > 0);
118	
119	// The window must lie inside the user VA range, or `map_page_in`'s `check_va`
120	// would reject every page of it with `MapError::OutOfRange`.
121	const _: () = assert!(USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_BASE + USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_SIZE <= USER_VA_TOP);
122	
123	// Every device VA must be page-aligned (a mapping granule) and lie wholly
124	// inside the window.
125	const _: () = assert!(TTY_UART_VA.is_multiple_of(USER_PAGE_SIZE));
126	const _: () = assert!(TTY_UART_VA >= USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_BASE);
127	const _: () =
128	    assert!(TTY_UART_VA + USER_PAGE_SIZE <= USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_BASE + USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_SIZE);
129	
130	// The ramdisk window's geometry, mirroring the device window's: one L1-slot
131	// boundary, no larger than one slot, a whole number of pages, inside the user VA
132	// range.
133	const _: () = assert!(RAMDISK_WINDOW_BASE.is_multiple_of(L1_SLOT_SIZE));
134	const _: () = assert!(RAMDISK_WINDOW_SIZE <= L1_SLOT_SIZE);
135	const _: () = assert!(RAMDISK_WINDOW_SIZE > 0);
136	const _: () = assert!(RAMDISK_WINDOW_SIZE.is_multiple_of(USER_PAGE_SIZE));

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Slice 5.7: the BDEV band, the `memory` ramdisk driver, and the root image.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Every marker below is identical with and without `boot-stubs` AND with and
# without the musl sysroot. That is what the FIXED image size buys: in the
# sysroot-absent build `kernel/build.rs` packs the 15 KB `worker` ELF as `hello`,
# so a content-sized image would make len/pages/blocks config-dependent -- the
# slice-5.5/5.6 "right in one config, vacuous in the other" trap.

# The kernel copies the archive's `rootfs` blob into fresh RAM frames and maps
# them into the memory driver's address space, page by page. Every field is a
# constant (uspace::RAMDISK_VA, rootfs::ROOTFS_IMAGE_BYTES / _BLOCKS), so all
# three are asserted. Unlike the tty device page these are ordinary RAM mapped
# Prot::RW_DATA -- no `prot.device` carve-out is involved anywhere.
[ramdisk] mem va=0x80000000 len=1048576 pages=256

# The driver announces itself on the kernel debug channel, exactly like the six
# SEF servers and the tty driver.
[diag memory] sef ready

# ...and then proves the mapping is real, complete, and holds this build's image.
# Two 32-byte SYS_COPY(SELF -> SELF) reads, so the driver never dereferences the
# mapping and a page the kernel failed to map is an EFAULT return rather than an
# EL0 data abort.
#
# `blocks=256` cross-checks the image header's OWN block count against the length
# SYS_GETINFO(GET_RAMDISK) reported -- two independently derived numbers, binding
# mkfs's geometry to the kernel's copy.
#
# `tail=1` is the 32-byte label read from the image's LAST block, whose text
# deliberately differs from the header's. It is the only thing in the whole boot
# that proves the copy loop reached the end of the blob: a loop that failed to
# advance would map 256 pages of block 0 and pass every header check.
#
# This is a DEVICE-level check, not a format-level one -- no superblock is
# decoded and `minixrs-mfs` is not a dependency of this driver, so Phase 6 can
# drop virtio-blk in under an unchanged MFS. `tools/mkfs-mfs`'s round-trip test
# `the_image_header_agrees_with_the_real_superblock` is what licenses checking the
# header instead; slice 5.8's READSUPER closes it for real.
[diag memory] ramdisk ok blocks=256 tail=1

# VFS drives the block device over BDEV_READ, resolving `memory` through DS
# rather than hard-coding boot_endpoint(MEM_PROC_NR) -- the 5.3 contract, with the
# same non-deterministic-publish caveat and the same distinguishable
# `bdev.ds FAIL` fallback.
[diag vfs] bdev.ds ok ep=

# A real read. The reply *is* the byte count, so a driver replying OK gives a
# different number here. This is also the first SUCCESSFUL `SAFECOPY_TO` anywhere
# in the tree -- every other use is a denial probe -- so it is what proves the
# kernel's CPF_WRITE + Prot::writable success path at all.
[diag vfs] bdev.read ok n=32

# The header bytes survived IPC + grant + safecopy...
[diag vfs] bdev.head ok match=1

# ...and the `block` field reached the right page. Head and tail do NOT subsume
# each other: a driver that ignored `block` would return the header for both, and
# the driver's own `tail=1` above proves the kernel's copy loop, not BDEV
# indexing. VFS zeroes its buffer between the two reads, so a read that moved
# nothing cannot pass this on stale bytes.
[diag vfs] bdev.tail ok match=1

# Nine refusals, each well-formed but for one field: minor 7 (-> ENXIO, the
# driver's own minor check), one block past the end (-> EINVAL, not EIO: a block
# device's size is known to its client), BDEV_MAX_IO + 1 bytes (-> EINVAL, the
# deliberate departure from CDEV's clamp -- a short block read is useless to a
# filesystem), a negative length (-> EINVAL, which unchecked would widen into a
# ~16 EiB u64), a grant issued to PM (-> EPERM, the kernel's `who_to` check), a
# CPF_READ-only grant used as a copy DESTINATION (-> EPERM: the access mask in the
# WRITE direction, which slice 5.3 never exercised), BDEV_WRITE (-> EROFS, not
# ENOSYS -- that distinction is the whole reason the request has a number), a
# request one past the band (-> ENOSYS, and the reply itself is the assertion: a
# dropped unknown would block VFS in its SENDREC forever and take every later
# marker with it), and SYS_GETINFO(GET_RAMDISK) issued by VFS (-> EPERM, the gate
# that keeps a VA mapped into one address space from being handed to another).
# A missing check makes its probe succeed and turns this into
# `bdev.deny FAIL <name>`.
[diag vfs] bdev.deny ok n=9

1	// SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause
2	// Copyright (c) 2025-2026 Kevin Barnard and minix.rs Contributors
3	//! Userland bootstrap: per-process address spaces with 8-bit ARMv8 ASIDs.
4	//!
5	//! Everything the kernel starts at EL0 is built here. Two shapes:
6	//!
7	//!   - **Boot servers and init**, loaded from the MXBI archive by
8	//!     [`load_boot_server`] — an ELF load plus one stack page. Slice 4.7
9	//!     factored the address-space half out as [`load_exec_image`], which
10	//!     `system::do_exec` reuses to re-image a live proc.
11	//!   - **Demo stubs A–D** (`boot-stubs` feature, default on), built by
12	//!     [`build_stub`] from raw blobs in `user_stub.S` — one code page, one
13	//!     stack page. They are the standing regression battery for the IPC
14	//!     primitives, SCHED delegation, VM page faults, and (as of slice 5.1)
15	//!     the fault-safe user copy; init and worker exercise none of that.
16	//!
17	//! Either way the proc gets its own [`AddrSpace`], frames come from
18	//! [`crate::mm`], contents are written through the HHDM
19	//! (`mm::phys_to_hhdm`) rather than the not-yet-active TTBR0, and the
20	//! resulting `(ttbr0_pa, asid)` is stored on the proc slot. The scheduler
21	//! ([`crate::proc::sched::schedule_next`]) installs that TTBR0 on every
22	//! EL1 → EL0 transition.
23	//!
24	//! The tree is owned by the proc slot from then on, not by an `AddrSpace`
25	//! value — hence the `mem::forget` at the end of each builder. Teardown goes
26	//! through `system::do_exit`, which frees leaf frames before the tables.
27	//!
28	//! No page is ever shared between stubs: each maps its own frame at its own
29	//! VA, so there is no kernel-global user mapping to reason about.
30	
31	use core::sync::atomic::Ordering;
32	
33	#[cfg(feature = "boot-stubs")]
34	use minixrs_kernel_shared::PrivId;
35	use minixrs_kernel_shared::ProcNr;
36	#[cfg(feature = "boot-stubs")]
37	use minixrs_kernel_shared::callnr::{KERNEL_CALL, SYS_GETINFO};

40	    RS_PROC_NR, SCHED_PROC_NR, STUB_A_PROC_NR, STUB_B_PROC_NR, STUB_C_PROC_NR, STUB_D_PROC_NR,
41	    SYSTEM, VM_PROC_NR, boot_endpoint,
42	};

47	};

50	use crate::arch::aarch64::asid::alloc_asid;

69	
70	/// VA at which stub A's code page is mapped.
71	#[cfg(feature = "boot-stubs")]

73	/// VA at which stub A's stack page is mapped.
74	#[cfg(feature = "boot-stubs")]
75	pub const USER_STACK_VA_A: u64 = 0x0080_0000; // 8 MiB

77	/// VA at which stub B's code page is mapped.
78	#[cfg(feature = "boot-stubs")]

80	/// VA at which stub B's stack page is mapped.

92	#[cfg(feature = "boot-stubs")]
93	pub const USER_CODE_VA_D: u64 = 0x0043_0000;
94	/// VA at which stub D's stack page is mapped.
95	#[cfg(feature = "boot-stubs")]
96	pub const USER_STACK_VA_D: u64 = 0x0083_0000;

98	// Stub D's heap VA (`0x0100_0000`) lives only in `user_stub.S`'s stub D blob
99	// and in the VM server's `region::HEAP_BASE` (slice 3.5): D issues `VM_BRK` to
100	// grow its heap, then touches it. The kernel needs no heap-window constant —
101	// faults route to VM, which gates them on its per-proc region table.
102	
103	// Stub proc numbers (slots 11..=15, just past the boot image) live in
104	// `kernel-shared::com` since slice 4.5 — PM's mproc table seeds them, so the
105	// kernel and PM must agree on one source.
106	
107	/// Privilege-table slots for the dedicated-priv stubs A–D. Boot image uses
108	/// 0..=15; 16, 17, 18, and 19 are the first free entries. The next slot up
109	/// (`proc::table::USER_PRIV_ID` = 20) is the shared USER priv that init (PID 1)
110	/// and every forked child use — no stub owns it.
111	#[cfg(feature = "boot-stubs")]
112	const STUB_A_PRIV_ID: PrivId = PrivId::new(16);
113	#[cfg(feature = "boot-stubs")]
114	const STUB_B_PRIV_ID: PrivId = PrivId::new(17);
115	#[cfg(feature = "boot-stubs")]
116	const STUB_C_PRIV_ID: PrivId = PrivId::new(18);
117	#[cfg(feature = "boot-stubs")]
118	const STUB_D_PRIV_ID: PrivId = PrivId::new(19);
119	
120	// SPSR_EL1 to install on each stub's `eret`. Matches slice 2.4: IRQs
121	// unmasked at EL0 (bit 7 = 0), debug + SError + FIQ masked. EL0t. Shared with
122	// `system::do_exec`, which resets an exec'd proc to the same EL0 state.
123	pub(crate) const STUB_SPSR_EL0: u64 = 0x340;
124	
125	// ----- EL0 stub blobs (linked into the kernel image by `user_stub.S`) ------
126	// Assembled only when `boot-stubs` is on — `kernel/build.rs` drops `user_stub.S`
127	// from the source list otherwise, so these externs must be gated to match.
128	
129	#[cfg(feature = "boot-stubs")]
130	unsafe extern "C" {
131	    static _user_stub_a_start: u8;
132	    static _user_stub_a_end: u8;
133	    static _user_stub_b_start: u8;
134	    static _user_stub_b_end: u8;
135	    static _user_stub_c_start: u8;
136	    static _user_stub_c_end: u8;
137	    static _user_stub_d_start: u8;
138	    static _user_stub_d_end: u8;
139	}
140	
141	/// VA at which each boot server's stack page is mapped. Distinct from the server
142	/// ELF segments (loaded from `0x0010_0000` up by `servers/*/user.ld`) and from
143	/// every EL0 stub VA. Shared across all servers: each has its own per-process
144	/// TTBR0, so the same low VA resolves to a distinct frame per server with no
145	/// collision (the same reason `user.ld`'s `0x0010_0000` base is shared).
146	const SERVER_STACK_VA: u64 = 0x0020_0000; // 2 MiB
147	
148	// ----- The device window must clear every VA declared above ------------------
149	//
150	// `kernel-shared::uspace` documents the whole user VA map and const-asserts the
151	// window's internal geometry, but the VAs it has to stay clear of are declared
152	// *here* (and, for the mmap arena, in `servers/vm/src/region.rs`, which carries
153	// its own guard plus a runtime cap). So the collision checks live here, where a

155	//
156	// Slice 5.7's ramdisk window needs **no entries of its own here**, and adding six
157	// redundant asserts would be a maintenance cost with no coverage: every assert

159	// `USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_BASE + USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_SIZE <= RAMDISK_WINDOW_BASE`
160	// makes the ramdisk's separation from each of these transitive.
161	
162	const _: () = assert!(USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_BASE > SERVER_STACK_VA + PAGE_SIZE as u64);
163	
164	#[cfg(feature = "boot-stubs")]
165	const _: () = assert!(USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_BASE > USER_STACK_VA_A + PAGE_SIZE as u64);

1	// SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause
2	// Copyright (c) 2025-2026 Kevin Barnard and minix.rs Contributors
3	// Assembles the per-arch entry path and exception vectors into the kernel.
4	//
5	// .S files go through clang (cross-targeted at the kernel triple) and the
6	// resulting .o files are passed straight to the linker via cargo:rustc-link-arg.
7	// We deliberately *avoid* the cc crate's static-library packaging because the
8	// linker's archive member resolution wouldn't pull in `_start` (it's only
9	// referenced via the linker-script `ENTRY` directive, not from any Rust
10	// symbol). Direct .o linkage sidesteps that, and it also dodges the
11	// macOS-ar/ELF-object mismatch entirely.
12	
13	use std::path::PathBuf;
14	use std::process::Command;
15	
16	fn main() {
17	    // The kernel is bare-metal only. It used to collapse to a no-op `main` on
18	    // host targets so `cargo check --workspace` stayed green, at the cost of
19	    // hiding every module behind `#[cfg(target_os = "none")]` — and therefore
20	    // from every lint gate.
21	    //
22	    // `forced-target` in Cargo.toml now pins this package to
23	    // aarch64-unknown-none for *every* cargo invocation, so in practice this
24	    // arm is unreachable. It stays as defense-in-depth: if that unstable
25	    // feature is ever dropped, this turns a cascade of `no_main` /
26	    // unset-`BOOT_IMAGE_PATH` errors into one actionable message, and it fires
27	    // before rustc runs.
28	    let target_os = std::env::var("CARGO_CFG_TARGET_OS").unwrap_or_default();
29	    if target_os != "none" {
30	        println!(
31	            "cargo::error=minixrs-kernel is a bare-metal crate (target_os = \"none\"); it \
32	             cannot be built for the host (got target_os = \"{target_os}\"). Build it with \
33	             `cargo kernel-aarch64`. If you are seeing this at all, the `forced-target` key \
34	             in kernel/Cargo.toml is not taking effect — check that cargo still supports the \
35	             unstable `per-package-target` feature."
36	        );
37	        return;
38	    }
39	
40	    let arch = std::env::var("CARGO_CFG_TARGET_ARCH").expect("CARGO_CFG_TARGET_ARCH unset");
41	    let out_dir = PathBuf::from(std::env::var_os("OUT_DIR").expect("OUT_DIR unset"));
42	
43	    // The `boot-stubs` feature (default-on) gates the demo stubs A–D. Build
44	    // scripts can't see `#[cfg(feature = ...)]`, so read the env var cargo sets
45	    // for enabled features. Off ⇒ skip `user_stub.S` assembly and build PM
46	    // stub-free so the two crates agree on `NR_STUB_PROCS`.
47	    let stubs = std::env::var_os("CARGO_FEATURE_BOOT_STUBS").is_some();
48	
49	    match arch.as_str() {
50	        "aarch64" => {
51	            let mut sources = vec![
52	                "src/arch/aarch64/entry.S",
53	                "src/arch/aarch64/vectors.S",
54	                "src/arch/aarch64/trap.S",
55	                "src/arch/aarch64/interrupt.S",
56	            ];
57	            if stubs {
58	                sources.push("src/arch/aarch64/user_stub.S");
59	            }
60	            for src in &sources {
61	                println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed={src}");
62	                let stem = std::path::Path::new(src)
63	                    .file_stem()
64	                    .unwrap()
65	                    .to_string_lossy();
66	                let obj = out_dir.join(format!("{stem}.o"));
67	                let status = Command::new("clang")
68	                    .args([
69	                        "--target=aarch64-unknown-none",
70	                        "-ffreestanding",
71	                        "-c",
72	                        src,
73	                        "-o",
74	                    ])
75	                    .arg(&obj)
76	                    .status()
77	                    .expect("failed to spawn clang");
78	                if !status.success() {
79	                    panic!("clang failed assembling {src}");
80	                }
81	                println!("cargo:rustc-link-arg={}", obj.display());
82	            }
83	            println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed=src/arch/aarch64/linker.ld");
84	
85	            // Build every boot server as a freestanding EL0 ELF, pack them into
86	            // the MXBI boot-image archive, and emit `BOOT_IMAGE_PATH` for
87	            // `boot_image` to `include_bytes!` (slice 4.2, generalizing the
88	            // slice-3.4 single-VM embed).
89	            build_boot_image(&out_dir, stubs);
90	        }
91	        "x86_64" => {
92	            // Phase 8 territory -- nothing to assemble yet.
93	        }
94	        other => panic!("unsupported target arch: {other}"),
95	    }
96	}
97	
98	/// Build every boot server, pack the resulting ELFs into the MXBI boot-image
99	/// archive in `OUT_DIR`, and emit `BOOT_IMAGE_PATH` so `boot_image` can
100	/// `include_bytes!` it (slice 4.2). Generalizes the slice-3.4 single-VM embed.
101	///
102	/// The server list is the single source of truth for which servers boot and at
103	/// which proc number; the proc numbers must match `kernel-shared/src/com.rs`.
104	/// VM is built first so it takes ASID 1 and is enqueued first (its
105	/// `RECEIVE(ANY)` blocks immediately, matching the pre-4.2 boot behavior).
106	fn build_boot_image(out_dir: &std::path::Path, stubs: bool) {
107	    let manifest =
108	        PathBuf::from(std::env::var("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR").expect("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR unset"));
109	    let workspace = manifest.parent().expect("kernel manifest has no parent");
110	
111	    // Libraries every server links against. Watched once (not per-server) so a
112	    // change re-runs build.rs and re-embeds. Each is watched as a directory so
113	    // cargo covers every submodule recursively — otherwise an edit to e.g. a new
114	    // `minixrs-ipc` module or DS request number would embed stale ELFs.
115	    for path in [
116	        workspace.join("minixrs-ipc/src"),
117	        workspace.join("server-rt/src"),
118	        workspace.join("kernel-shared/src"),
119	        workspace.join("minixrs-abi-note/src"),
120	        workspace.join("tools/targets/aarch64-unknown-minixrs.json"),
121	    ] {
122	        println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed={}", path.display());
123	    }
124	
125	    // (cargo package, crate dir, boot proc number). Proc numbers come from
126	    // `kernel-shared/src/com.rs`; the archive carries them so the loader writes
127	    // the right proc slot. `worker` is packed with proc_nr -1
128	    // (`com::EXEC_ONLY_PROC_NR`): it is not a boot server — the loader skips any
129	    // negative proc_nr — but it is resolvable by name for `SYS_EXEC` (slice 4.7).
130	    let servers: [(&str, std::path::PathBuf, i32); 10] = [
131	        ("minixrs-vm", workspace.join("servers/vm"), 7), // VM_PROC_NR
132	        ("minixrs-ds", workspace.join("servers/ds"), 5), // DS_PROC_NR
133	        // The drivers sit between DS and VFS on purpose. DS must come first so
134	        // every later server's `DS_PUBLISH` lands; each driver should reach its
135	        // receive loop before its first client, which is VFS today (slice 5.3's
136	        // console demo and 5.7's block demo) and stays VFS for 5.4's fd 1/2 and
137	        // 5.6's musl `printf`. MEM specifically precedes VFS so 5.7's demo lookup
138	        // — and 5.8's MFS lookup, which is the one that matters — resolve through
139	        // DS deterministically by construction rather than by luck.
140	        ("minixrs-tty", workspace.join("drivers/tty"), 4), // TTY_PROC_NR
141	        ("minixrs-vfs", workspace.join("servers/vfs"), 1), // VFS_PROC_NR
142	        ("minixrs-memory", workspace.join("drivers/memory"), 3), // MEM_PROC_NR
143	        // MUTATION 4: memory packed after vfs
144	        ("minixrs-sched", workspace.join("servers/sched"), 9), // SCHED_PROC_NR
145	        ("minixrs-rs", workspace.join("servers/rs"), 2),   // RS_PROC_NR
146	        ("minixrs-pm", workspace.join("servers/pm"), 0),   // PM_PROC_NR
147	        ("minixrs-init", workspace.join("userland/init"), 10), // INIT_PROC_NR — PID 1
148	        ("minixrs-worker", workspace.join("userland/worker"), -1), // EXEC_ONLY_PROC_NR
149	    ];

### Slice 5.7: BDEV band + `memory` ramdisk driver + `tools/mkfs-mfs` + rootfs blob ◀ next

**Goal:** D3 — a block-device story with a real MFS image behind it.

**Scope:** `fs/mfs` library half first: MinixFS v3 on-disk structs
(superblock/inode/dirent, 4 KiB blocks) + pure readers, host-tested.
`tools/mkfs-mfs` host tool builds `rootfs.img` from a manifest
(`/bin/hello` from 5.6's build, `/etc/motd`); round-trip host tests against
the mfs readers. `kernel/build.rs` runs mkfs and packs the image as
(`rootfs`, −1). Kernel boot: copy blob to RAM frames, map RW into MEM's AS;
new `SYS_GETINFO` selector returns `(va, len)`. `drivers/memory` becomes a
real server (roster +1, proc_nr 3): serves `BDEV_RQ_BASE = 0xA00`
`BDEV_READ`/`BDEV_WRITE {minor, block, count, granter, grant_id}` against
the mapped image via safecopy.

**Proof:** MEM's init `diag_print`s image size + superblock-magic check
(`[as]` roster grows to 13); BDEV round-trip is exercised by host tests here
and by live IPC in 5.8.

### Slice 5.8: MFS server (read-only) + FS band + VFS mount/open/read

**Goal:** files readable through the full VFS→MFS→BDEV→ramdisk stack.

**Scope:** `fs/mfs` server half (roster +1, proc_nr 6): SEF loop serving
`FS_RQ_BASE = 0x900` — READSUPER (via BDEV_READ to MEM), LOOKUP (whole-path
per D13), PUTNODE, READ (data moved by magic grant direct to the
requester's buffer), STAT-lite. VFS: lazy root mount on first open;

### Slice 5.7: BDEV band + `memory` ramdisk driver + `tools/mkfs-mfs` + rootfs blob ◀ ready (branch `feature/slice-5.7-bdev-ramdisk`, pending merge)

**Goal:** D3 — a block-device story with a real MFS image behind it.

**Scope:** `fs/mfs` library half first: MinixFS v3 on-disk structs
(superblock/inode/dirent, 4 KiB blocks) + pure readers, host-tested.
`tools/mkfs-mfs` host tool builds `rootfs.img` from a manifest
(`/bin/hello` from 5.6's build, `/etc/motd`); round-trip host tests against
the mfs readers. `kernel/build.rs` runs mkfs and packs the image as
(`rootfs`, −1). Kernel boot: copy blob to RAM frames, map RW into MEM's AS;
new `SYS_GETINFO` selector returns `(va, len)`. `drivers/memory` becomes a
real server (roster +1, proc_nr 3): serves `BDEV_RQ_BASE = 0xA00`
`BDEV_READ`/`BDEV_WRITE` against the mapped image via safecopy.

**Proof:** the `[as]` roster grows to 13; `[ramdisk] mem va=… len=… pages=…`
from the kernel's copy loop; `[diag memory] ramdisk ok blocks=256 tail=1`;
and a live VFS client exercising `bdev.{ds,read,head,tail,deny}`.

#### As built — five differences from the sketch above

1. **No `granter` field in the payload, and no grant offset.** The sketch's
   `{minor, block, count, granter, grant_id}` would have made every
   grant-holding block driver a confused deputy. The driver takes the granter
   from the kernel-stamped `m_source`, the 5.2/5.3 rule; the offset is absent
   because every client through 5.9 grants a buffer whose block starts at 0.
   The payload is `{minor, grant, len, block}`, mirroring `CDEV_WRITE`.
2. **A fixed-size image (`ROOTFS_IMAGE_BLOCKS = 256`, 1 MiB), not a
   content-sized one.** In the musl-sysroot-absent fallback `build_hello`
   returns the 15 KB *worker* ELF, so a content-sized image would make every
   size-derived marker config-dependent — the 5.5/5.6 "right in one config,
   vacuous in the other" trap. Oversizing is a build failure
   (`MkfsError::TooBig`) naming one constant.
3. **`/etc/pattern` (40 KiB) is mandatory, not filler.** `/bin/hello` is
   ~200 KB = 49 blocks and forces the single-indirect zone arm — but in the
   fallback config it is 15 KB = 4 blocks, *inside* the 7 direct zones, so
   both the arm and mkfs's indirect writer would be dead in exactly the
   config CI's non-QEMU jobs build. A constant-size file past the boundary
   keeps them live in both.
4. **MEM's init check is device-level, not format-level.** A superblock-magic
   check would make a *block* driver depend on the *filesystem format* crate,
   which Phase 6 then has to unwind when virtio-blk replaces MEM under an
   unchanged MFS. Instead mkfs writes a 32-byte image header into block 0's
   unused boot block (bytes 0..1024, which MFS never reads) and a 32-byte
   tail label into a reserved last zone; MEM verifies those, and format-level
   facts are verified by a client *through a real BDEV round trip* — strictly
   stronger, since MEM reading its own mapping proves only that the copy loop
   ran. The header/superblock agreement is a mkfs round-trip test.
5. **The image-header ABI lives in `kernel-shared::rootfs`, not in
   `tools/mkfs-mfs`.** mkfs writes those bytes, MEM and VFS read them, and
   none of the three may depend on the others — the same reason
   `com::ROOTFS_MODULE_NAME` is shared. `image.rs` re-exports them so the
   writer's own constants still read locally.

Also: `BDEV_WRITE` is defined now and answers `EROFS` rather than `ENOSYS`
(which is already the unknown-`m_type` answer, so reusing it would make
"doesn't know about writes" and "knows and refuses" indistinguishable), and an
over-long or out-of-range request is `EINVAL` rather than a short read — a
deliberate departure from CDEV, because a filesystem cannot interpret half a
block.

### Slice 5.8: MFS server (read-only) + FS band + VFS mount/open/read ◀ next

lines: - **Errno ABI + generated C headers (slice 5.0):** `kernel-shared/src/error.rs` has two bands (phase-5 decision D7) — the **POSIX block, magnitudes `1..=40`**, at classic book-era MINIX values, which are identical to Linux/musl's (that identity is the whole point: musl's stock `bits/errno.h` and `syscall_ret.c`'s `r > -4096UL` work unmodified), and the **MINIX-specific IPC band at `>= 200`**, taking modern MINIX 3 `sys/sys/errno.h` values (`ENOTREADY` 201, `EDEADSRCDST` 202, `EDONTREPLY` 203, `EGENERIC` 204, `ELOCKED` 208 … plus `EBADSRCDST` 216, the one name modern MINIX lacks — it spells that condition `EBADEPT`). Nothing may land in the `41..=199` gap, where musl defines errnos minix.rs has *not* adopted. Constants are stored **negated**; an `errnos!` macro takes the positive magnitude and emits both the `pub const` and `pub const ALL: &[(&str, i32)]` — `ALL` is the single source of truth for the header generator, the `const _` band/distinctness guards, and the host tests, so **add an errno by adding one line to the macro invocation, never by hand-editing a second list**. `tools/gen-c-headers` (package `minixrs-gen-c-headers`, first host/`std` crate in the workspace; lib holds the renderers + tests, `main.rs` is argv/IO only and is Sonar-coverage-excluded via `tools/**/src/main.rs`) prints `include/minixrs/{ipc,com,callnr,errno}.h` from the live constants; **the headers are a build artifact under `target/` and are never committed** (D8 — drift is impossible by construction, and CI asserts nothing was written into the tree). Four things to preserve when extending it: generated C uses **C11 keywords** (`_Static_assert`, `_Alignas` on the struct's *first member* — C11 forbids it on a type declaration — and `_Alignof`), never GNU attributes; `minixrs/ipc.h` **includes nothing** (`offsetof` comes from `__builtin_offsetof` under the private name `_MINIXRS_OFFSETOF`, because Apple's clang redirects `<stddef.h>` to the system header for any `*-musl` triple and would break the hermetic `-nostdlibinc -ffreestanding` CI check); every process gets **both** `<NAME>_PROC_NR` and `<NAME>_EP` (they differ for kernel tasks — `SYSTEM_PROC_NR` is −2, `SYSTEM_EP` is 32766 — and the header `_Static_assert`s the C decode macro against the Rust-computed endpoints); and `minixrs/errno.h` **asserts but never defines** the POSIX block, behind `#ifdef MINIXRS_ABI_CHECK_POSIX_ERRNO`, since CI has no musl sysroot and a host `<errno.h>` disagrees (Darwin `EDEADLK` is 11) — slice 5.6's `tools/build-musl.sh` must define that macro to make the value check real. `abi-selftest.c` exists because a header is never a translation unit, so without a `.c` file none of the `_Static_assert`s would ever fire

- **Fault-safe user access + the debug channel (slice 5.1):** the kernel **never dereferences a user VA**, not even the active TTBR0's. Every byte in or out of a user address space goes through `kernel/src/mm/uaccess.rs` — `copy_from_user_as(ttbr0_pa, va, dst)` / `copy_to_user_as(ttbr0_pa, va, src)` / `probe_user_range(ttbr0_pa, va, len, write)` — which page-chunks the range, resolves each page with the new `addrspace::walk_pt_in(ttbr0_pa, va) -> Option<(u64, Prot)>` (the missing member of the `map_page_in`/`unmap_page_in`/`walk_leaves` free-function family; `AddrSpace::walk_pt` delegates to it), and `memcpy`s through the frame's HHDM alias. Consequences to preserve: an unmapped page is a walk miss returning **`EFAULT`, not an EL1 abort** — so **no exception-fixup table is needed or wanted** (D5 rejected the Linux `extable` approach); the copy is **address-space-independent**, so `flush_deliver_msg` can write a receiver's buffer before its TTBR0 is installed (the TTBR0-before-flush ordering in `sched::schedule_next` is no longer load-bearing, only `eret` needs it); `copy_to_user_as` must **check `Prot::writable`**, because the HHDM alias is a kernel mapping that the MMU's EL0 permission bits do not police; and writes are **all-or-nothing** (probe first) since a 104-byte `Message` is only 8-aligned and really can straddle two pages. Slice 5.2's grant engine builds on these primitives rather than re-deriving them. `user_va_ok` stays as the cheap range/alignment pre-gate; the page arithmetic (`page_chunks` / `PageChunk` / `USER_PAGE_SIZE`) lives in `kernel-shared/src/message.rs` beside it because the kernel crate has no `#[cfg(test)]`. `ipc/message.rs` carries **zero `unsafe`** — messages stage through a `[u8; 104]` — so all raw-pointer work is in `mm::uaccess` alone. Error routing: `EFAULT` to the caller's `x0` via `do_ipc` for the three immediate sites, and to a blocked receiver's **parked `x0`** (`p.regs.x[0] = e as i64 as u64` — the MINIX `retreg` idiom `do_exit::unblock_dependents` uses) for the deferred flush, which also sets/clears the previously-unused `MF_MSGFAILED`. Both traces are **uncounted** (`[efault] proc=… nr=… call=… va=…`, `[efault deliver] proc=… nr=… va=…`) so they are stable boot markers, unlike the sampled `[ipc {n}]` form; the `do_ipc` one keys on `result == EFAULT`, which is unambiguous because nothing else in the kernel produces it. **`SYS_DIAGCTL` is the servers' debug channel** (D2) — servers run at EL0 with no console, and this must keep working while grants/TTY/VFS are under construction, so the text rides **inline in the payload** (subcode `0..4`, len `4..8`, up to `DIAG_TEXT_MAX = 88` bytes from `DIAG_TEXT_OFF = 8`) and needs no user-copy machinery. `kernel/src/system/do_diagctl.rs` prints one line per call as `[diag <name>] <text>`, where `<name>` is the caller's kernel-known `Proc::name` (never payload data, so a server can only identify itself) and text is sanitized to printable ASCII (so one call is always exactly one line — the `grep -aF` marker contract depends on it). `server-rt::diag_print` is the client, chunking longer strings; it is called from **`sef_startup`**, so all six SEF servers emit `[diag <name>] sef ready` at boot. Adding a stub is discouraged: `NR_STUB_PROCS` feeds `FORK_POOL_BASE`, so a fifth stub shifts init's forked children 15 → 16 and breaks checked-in markers — put new probe behavior in an existing stub's prologue (5.1 used stub A's)

- **Grants — the governed cross-address-space copy (slice 5.2, D4):** a granting process keeps its `GrantEntry` table **in its own address space** and registers `(addr, entries)` with `SYS_SETGRANT`; `SYS_SAFECOPY` reads the entry back out of the *granter's* address space on every call, so a granter revokes by writing its own memory and the kernel caches nothing that could go stale. The ABI is `kernel-shared/src/grant.rs` — flat `#[repr(C)]` `GrantEntry` (flags/seq/who_to/who_from/addr/len, 32 bytes, layout pinned by `offset_of!` asserts because the kernel decodes it from raw bytes), MINIX's CPF flag values, and `GRANT_SHIFT = 20` id packing (`grant_id`/`grant_idx`/`grant_seq`). The engine is one new function beside the 5.1 trio, `mm::uaccess::copy_between_as(src_ttbr0, src_va, dst_ttbr0, dst_va, len)`: probe both ranges, then walk-and-`memcpy` per `dual_page_chunks` — **all-or-nothing on the destination**, and its `Prot::writable` check is load-bearing (a granter may *lie* about writability, and the HHDM alias is a kernel mapping the MMU's EL0 bits do not police). `verify_grant` (`system/do_safecopy.rs`) checks, in MINIX's order: `okendpt` the granter, table registered + idx in range, entry reads back (a walk miss is hidden as **`EPERM`, not `EFAULT`**, so a grantee cannot probe the granter's address space), `CPF_USED|CPF_VALID`, `seq` matches the id, requested access ⊆ flags, `who_to` == caller's *stored endpoint*, `offset + bytes <= len`. `CPF_DIRECT` resolves the memory to the granter; `CPF_MAGIC` resolves it to `who_from` and additionally requires the granter's `Priv::flags & SYS_PROC` (minix.rs's stand-in for MINIX's hardcoded VFS/MIB list); `CPF_INDIRECT` is a documented `EINVAL`. `SYS_COPY` is the same engine with no grant — `resolve_target` on both endpoints (`SELF` works), `k_call_mask` is the only gate, the `do_vmctl` trust stance. All three are routed from the **target-taking `match`** in `kernel_call_dispatch`, `SYS_SETGRANT` included: it is caller-local in effect but needs `&mut Priv`, which `dispatch_caller_local` cannot hand out. 225:- **C on minix.rs — the musl port, the sysroot, and the ABI freeze (slice 5.6, milestone A):** the libc is a **git submodule at `external/musl`** → `minixrs/musl-minixrs`, tracking branch **`minixrs`** (the port; `main` is a pristine upstream mirror with nothing on it), based on tag **`v1.2.6`**. The old `KevinBarnard/musl-minix` is archived and nothing was carried over. The fork's whole delta is `arch/aarch64/syscall_arch.h` + `src/minixrs/` + a brand block in `crt/crt1.c` + `MINIXRS.md`, and staying that small is the design goal — **musl globs `src/*/`, so `src/minixrs/` needs no Makefile edit**. Every `__syscallN` calls `__minixrs_syscall`, which switches on the *Linux* number musl still emits and issues a server round-trip (`writev`/`write` → `VFS_WRITE`, `exit`/`exit_group` → `PM_EXIT`, `set_tid_address` → 1, `ioctl` → `-ENOTTY`, everything else `-ENOSYS`); musl's ~297 call sites stay untouched, which is what lets ~1900 files rebase for free. `syscall_ret.c` is untouched because D7's magnitudes (`1..=40`, `>=200`) all sit inside its `> -4096UL` window. **`ioctl` → `-ENOTTY` is load-bearing**: it makes `__stdout_write` set `f->lbf = -1`, so stdout is **fully buffered** and `printf` only reaches the console via `exit()`'s `__stdio_exit` — the milestone marker therefore proves the flush path too. Six syscalls suffice only because of startup facts that must be **re-verified, never assumed, on any musl bump** (all re-read against v1.2.6, recorded in the fork's `MINIXRS.md`): `__init_libc` early-returns past its `ppoll` when `AT_UID`/`AT_GID`/`AT_SECURE` are absent (they read 0); `__init_ssp(NULL)` derives the canary arithmetically; `__init_tp`'s only syscall is `set_tid_address` (`__set_thread_area` is `msr tpidr_el0` inline asm since v1.2.6) and it **walks `libc.auxv`**, so the auxv must stay `AT_NULL`-terminated; `__init_tls` uses static `builtin_tls` absent a `PT_TLS` (so no `mmap`) and walks 5.5's `AT_PHDR`/`AT_PHNUM`/`AT_PHENT`. **`tools/build-musl.sh`** builds an out-of-tree sysroot into `target/musl-sysroot` (the submodule work tree stays **pristine** — the `c-headers` job asserts a clean `git status`), keyed by a `.stamp` of submodule SHA + toolchain; `RANLIB` is **`llvm-ar s`**, because the pinned toolchain ships `llvm-ar` but **not** `llvm-ranlib`. It also runs the **real D7 errno *value* check** 5.0 deferred here — the opt-in POSIX block compiled against the fork's own `bits/errno.h` under `-nostdinc -isystem <sysroot>/include`; the CI `c-headers` job keeps only the hermetic stand-in check. `userland/hello` is **not a cargo crate** — `hello.c` + `hello.ld` compiled by clang and linked by `rust-lld` inside `kernel/build.rs::build_hello`, packed under proc_nr `-1` like `worker`. **The fallback presence-checks the SYSROOT (`.stamp`), not the submodule**, and packs the `worker` ELF *under the name* `hello` with a `cargo::warning` — checking the submodule would let a fresh clone trigger a multi-minute libc build from inside a build script. That substitution is why `worker`'s `ARGV0_NAMES` is the **set** `{worker, hello}` rather than one literal: it checks the exact `argv[0]` bytes the kernel wrote, so the hardcoded `b"worker"` made a *missing sysroot* print `worker: stack FAIL` — a **forbidden** marker — making an absent optional dependency indistinguishable from a broken exec ABI. **Boot the fallback config when you change it**; two readings of the name-level substitution missed this and only running it caught it. musl's `vfprintf` needs soft-float **binary128** builtins (`__multf3`/`__floatsitf`/…; aarch64 `long double` is IEEE quad) which musl's configure finds no library for: they come from **`compiler_builtins` as built by `-Zbuild-std` for `aarch64-unknown-minixrs`** — the *prebuilt* `aarch64-unknown-none` rlib in the rustup sysroot does **not** export the C-ABI names, so glob the nested target dir, never the sysroot. `hello.ld` is `worker/user.ld` plus what only a musl link brings — `.init`/`.fini` (they define the `_init`/`_fini` `crt1.c` passes to `__libc_start_main`), `.init_array`/`.fini_array` with bracketing symbols, `.got`, `.data.rel.ro` — because **an orphan section past the last `PT_LOAD` is a silent load failure**; the `FILEHDR PHDRS` idiom is mandatory (not just an auxv nicety as for Rust: `__init_tls` dereferences `AT_PHDR`). # Drivers

A **driver** in minix.rs is an ordinary user-space process that happens to own a
piece of hardware. It is not a special kind of kernel module and it holds no
kernel privilege beyond a `k_call_mask` bit or two — it is a
`#![no_std]`/`#![no_main]` ELF, loaded from the MXBI archive into its own address
space, driving a SEF receive loop exactly like [a server](../servers/overview.md).

What separates a driver from a server is one page in its address space that no
other process has: the device's memory-mapped registers. Everything interesting
about this chapter follows from that page.

As of Phase 5 there is exactly one driver, **TTY** (`drivers/tty/`), the console.
The VirtIO block, network, and console drivers under `drivers/` are still empty
placeholders (Phase 6), and so is `drivers/driver-rt` — the shared driver runtime
they will eventually use.

## The device window

The kernel and user space agree on a range of virtual addresses reserved for MMIO,
declared in `kernel-shared/src/uspace.rs`:

```rust
pub const USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_BASE: u64 = 0x4000_0000;   // 1 GiB — one whole L1 slot
pub const USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_SIZE: u64 = 0x0100_0000;   // 16 MiB
pub const TTY_UART_VA: u64 = USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_BASE;   // page 0 of the window
```

That module is deliberately separate from `message.rs`, which holds every other
shared constant. The rest of `kernel-shared` describes a *message* ABI — bytes on
the wire between two processes, where a wrong value gets a request rejected. This
is an *address* ABI: the kernel installs a mapping and user code dereferences it,
with no message in between, and a wrong value is a data abort.

`0x4000_0000` is chosen to be a whole L1 slot (1 GiB-aligned, so the window costs
exactly one L1 entry) and to sit clear of every occupied user VA — server images
at 1 MiB, server stacks at 2 MiB, demo-stub code and stacks at 4 and 8 MiB, VM's
heap origin at 16 MiB, VM's mmap arena at 32 MiB.

Two of those grow on request, and a compile-time assert on their *bases* would prove
only where they start. The heap's end is whatever `brk` last asked for, and the mmap
arena is a bump allocator that never reuses addresses — so `servers/vm/src/region.rs`
bounds both with a runtime `REGION_LIMIT` check (`ENOMEM` past it) rather than
trusting the 992 MiB of slack. That matters even though nothing is exploitable
today: the window's whole purpose is to be kernel-owned in *every* address space, so
Phase 6 can pre-map a device page into any driver without first asking whether VM
already promised that VA to the process's heap.

## The boot pre-map

TTY has no way to *ask* for its register page. There is no `VMCTL_MAP_PHYS`
subcall — a subcall letting a user-space server name an arbitrary physical address

## The BDEV protocol and the `memory` ramdisk

Block drivers answer requests in the `BDEV_RQ_BASE = 0xA00` band — between VFS
(`0x800`) and CDEV (`0xB00`), with `0x900` reserved for the VFS↔FS band. Two
requests are defined:

| Field | Payload offset | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| minor | `0..4` (i32) | which device; `BDEV_MINOR_RAMDISK = 0` is the boot image |
| grant id | `4..8` (i32) | names the client's buffer |
| length | `8..12` (i32) | bytes requested; at most `BDEV_MAX_IO` = one block |
| block | `16..24` (u64) | which block of the device |

`BDEV_READ` fills the client's buffer (so the grant needs `CPF_WRITE`, and the
driver pushes with `SAFECOPY_TO`). `BDEV_WRITE` is defined and answers `EROFS`.

Most of that table repeats CDEV's rules — no granter field, and the reply `m_type`
*is* the byte count. Three things are deliberately different:

**An over-long request is `EINVAL`, not a short read.** A short *write* is a POSIX
contract every client already loops over. A short *block read* is useless: a
filesystem cannot interpret half a block, so clamping would push a retry loop into
every caller for nothing.

**An out-of-range block is `EINVAL`, not `EIO`.** A block device's size is known to
its client — MFS reads it from the superblock's `s_zones` — so asking past the end
is a caller bug. `EIO` stays reserved for Phase 6's real media errors, where the
request was well-formed and the *device* failed.

**`BDEV_WRITE` answers `EROFS`, not `ENOSYS`.** `ENOSYS` is already the
unknown-`m_type` answer, so reusing it would make "this driver has never heard of
writes" and "this driver knows about writes and refuses them" indistinguishable to
a client. Keeping the arm dispatched also keeps it probed, and slice 5.10 changes
one line inside it.

### Where the blocks come from

`kernel/build.rs` builds a MinixFS v3 image at compile time (`tools/mkfs-mfs`,
called as a build-dependency library) and packs it into the MXBI archive as a
**non-ELF blob** named `rootfs`. At boot the kernel copies it, page by page, into
freshly allocated frames and maps them into the `memory` driver's address space —
in the same `load_boot_server` arm the UART page uses, and for the same reason: the
driver has no way to ask.

The window is declared beside the device window, and is **ordinary RAM**:

```rust
pub const RAMDISK_WINDOW_BASE: u64 = 0x8000_0000;   // 2 GiB — one whole L1 slot
pub const RAMDISK_WINDOW_SIZE: u64 = 0x0040_0000;   // 4 MiB
pub const RAMDISK_VA: u64 = RAMDISK_WINDOW_BASE;    // page 0 of the window
```

Two choices there are worth stating. It sits **above** the device window on
purpose: `region::REGION_LIMIT` is the base of the *lowest* kernel-owned window, so
placing every new window above that low-water mark means VM needs no edit at all
when one is added — and `assert!(USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_BASE + USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_SIZE
<= RAMDISK_WINDOW_BASE)` is what keeps that true. And the pages are mapped
`Prot::RW_DATA`, not device: none of the `prot.device` machinery above applies, and
these frames take the ordinary `free_frame` path in every leaf sweep. (RW rather
than RO so slice 5.10's write path is a change in the driver rather than in the
kernel.)

The 4 MiB size comes from the *format*, not from today's image: seven direct zones
plus one single-indirect block address `7 + 1024` zones at 4 KiB, which is 4.03 MiB.
An image that fits the window is therefore an image `fs/mfs`'s reader can address
without a double-indirect arm.

The driver learns where it is through a new `SYS_GETINFO` selector, `GET_RAMDISK`,
which returns `(va, len)` and is **gated on the caller being `MEM_PROC_NR`**: the
ramdisk is mapped into exactly one address space, so the VA is meaningless — and
actively misleading — anywhere else.

### The driver has no `unsafe` block

`drivers/memory/` never dereferences its mapping. Client transfers go through
`SYS_SAFECOPY`, and even the boot self-check reads the image through
`SYS_COPY(SELF → SELF)` rather than a raw load. So a page the kernel failed to map
surfaces as an `EFAULT` *return value* from a kernel call — a better diagnostic
than TTY's equivalent, which is an EL0 data abort — and there is no MMIO sibling
module to exclude from coverage.

The self-check is deliberately **device-level, not format-level**: it reads a
32-byte image header that `mkfs-mfs` writes into block 0's boot block (bytes
`0..1024`, which MinixFS never reads), never a superblock. A block driver that
decoded a superblock would depend on the filesystem format, which is precisely the
dependency Phase 6 has to unwind when virtio-blk replaces the ramdisk. What
licenses that shortcut is a host test in `tools/mkfs-mfs` asserting the header's
three fields equal the real superblock's.

It also reads a **tail label** from the image's reserved last block, whose text
differs from the header's. That is not decoration: a kernel copy loop that failed to
advance would map 256 pages of block 0 and pass every header check. The tail is the
only thing in the boot that proves the copy reached the end of the blob — confirmed
by mutation, where sourcing every page from block 0 moved exactly one marker,
`ramdisk FAIL tail label`.

### What the boot log proves

```
[ramdisk] mem va=0x80000000 len=1048576 pages=256
[diag memory] ramdisk ok blocks=256 tail=1
[diag vfs] bdev.ds ok ep=3
[diag vfs] bdev.read ok n=32
[diag vfs] bdev.head ok match=1
[diag vfs] bdev.tail ok match=1
[diag vfs] bdev.deny ok n=9
```

`blocks=256` cross-checks the header's own block count against the length
`GET_RAMDISK` reported — two independently derived numbers, binding the build-time
image geometry to the kernel's runtime copy.

VFS then drives the protocol as the first client, and `bdev.read` matters beyond
this driver: it is the first **successful** `SAFECOPY_TO` anywhere in the tree.
Every other use of that direction is a denial probe, so until now the kernel's
`CPF_WRITE` + `Prot::writable` success path had never run. `bdev.head` and
`bdev.tail` do not subsume each other — a driver that ignored the `block` field
would return the header for both — and the nine refusals include the one grant check
slice 5.3 could not reach: a `CPF_READ`-only grant used as a copy *destination*.

Every one of those markers is identical with and without the `boot-stubs` feature
**and** with and without the musl sysroot. That is what the fixed 1 MiB image size
buys: in the sysroot-absent build the archive packs a 15 KB `worker` ELF under the
name `hello`, so a content-sized image would make every size-derived marker
config-dependent — passing in one configuration and proving nothing in the other.

Slice 5.7 is implemented and verified on `feature/slice-5.7-bdev-ramdisk`. Nothing is committed — the tree is yours to review.

## What shipped

**ABI** — `BDEV_RQ_BASE = 0xA00` between VFS and CDEV, `{minor, grant, len, block}` (no granter field, no grant-offset field), `BDEV_WRITE` → `EROFS`, `GET_RAMDISK = 64`. The four stale "BDEV at `0x900`" comments are corrected. The C header gains the band; `bands_are_in_ascending_numeric_order` and the re-chained `_Static_assert`s pass.

**Format + writer** — `fs/mfs` (superblock/inode/dirent/layout/read, `no_std`, `forbid(unsafe_code)`, one dependency, I/O-free) and `tools/mkfs-mfs`, called as a build-dependency library from `kernel/build.rs`. 22 round-trip tests read a real image back through the same decoders slice 5.8's server will use.

**Kernel** — ramdisk window at 2 GiB, a `nr == MEM_PROC_NR` pre-map arm beside TTY's, and the `MEM_PROC_NR`-gated getinfo selector. `pack_mxbi` gained its `u32` cast guards.

**Driver** — `drivers/memory` with zero `unsafe` blocks: client transfers via `sys_safecopy`, self-check via `sys_copy(SELF→SELF)`.

## Verification

`fmt --check`, `clippy --workspace --all-targets`, and both kernel clippy configs are clean. 268 host tests pass. Three boots — default, `--no-default-features`, and the musl-sysroot-absent fallback — all carry every 5.7 marker identically; `check-boot-log.sh` passes all 72 on the default config. The stub-free run's only misses are the four stub markers, which is pre-existing. The C-header gate compiles and writes nothing into the tree.

Six mutations, all restored and `diff -q`'d clean (`grep -rn MUTATION` finds only the CLAUDE.md rule that describes the procedure).

## Three things you should know

**`bdev.deny ok n=9`, not `n=8`.** The plan's marker table says 8, then describes a ninth probe. I ran all nine and made the count match the marker, since a count that disagreed with the probe list would be the exact class of vacuous marker the plan warns about.

**The image-header ABI went into `kernel-shared::rootfs`, not `tools/mkfs-mfs/src/image.rs`.** The plan puts those constants in mkfs but also forbids MEM and VFS from depending on `minixrs-mfs` — and both need to read the header. `kernel-shared` is the one crate all three already depend on, the same resolution `ROOTFS_MODULE_NAME` uses. `image.rs` re-exports them, so the plan's names still resolve there.

**Mutation 4 did not move its marker.** Packing `memory` after `vfs` left `bdev.ds ok` intact — the DS publish still won the race on this host. That is a finding about the property, not the marker: publish-before-retrieve genuinely is luck, which is why the fallback exists. I got the `bdev.ds FAIL rc=-3 fallback=3` observation from mutation 1 instead, which also confirmed the demo's last-in-prologue placement (it took 5.4's init markers down with it, and left 5.3's standing).

CLAUDE.md:248:Mutation tests (the 5.1/5.2/5.3 standard: apply, observe the named marker move, revert) run against an **uncommitted** working tree, so never revert one with `git checkout <file>` — copy the files to the scratchpad first and restore from there, then `diff -q` each back and `grep -rn MUTATION` to prove nothing leaked into the PR. A mutation that fails to **compile** is indistinguishable from one that worked: `kernel/build.rs` panics on the nested server build, the log holds no kernel output at all, and `check-boot-log.sh` reports every marker MISSING. Review addressed. Here's how each finding landed:

**1. `pack_mxbi` total-size truncation — real bug, fixed.** Correct catch. The loop checked `offset` *before* adding the module's length, so the final total was the one value it couldn't cover: the last module can start inside the u32 range and end past it. `total_size` is itself a u32 header field, so the cast could truncate the archive's own recorded size while every per-record assert passed. Added the post-loop assert.

**2. `BDEV_WRITE` skipping validation — fixed now, not deferred.** Worth doing immediately for a reason beyond consistency: my own module docs and the CLAUDE.md bullet both claim slice 5.10 "changes one line inside one arm." With a bare `EROFS` that was an overstatement — 5.10 would have had to *add* the validation. `do_write` now runs the shared validator and refuses only a request this device could have served, so a write to minor 7 gets `ENXIO` rather than an assertion about a device that doesn't exist.

That created an unprobed outcome, so I added a tenth denial probe (`write-bad-minor` → `ENXIO`) and mutation-tested it: reverting to bare `EROFS` gives `bdev.deny FAIL write-bad-minor rc=-30` and the marker disappears. Marker is now `n=10`; expected file updated.

**3. `fs/mfs/src/main.rs` — declined, deliberately.** The plan is explicit that it stays untouched so the `fs/**/src/main.rs` Sonar exclusion lands with the MFS server in 5.8. It also predates this slice. Deleting it now would mean re-adding it plus the exclusion in 5.8, to save one `fn main() {}` host build.

**4. Inverted assert message — not inverted, but reworded.** The message prints only on failure, and failure means `GET_RAMDISK < 32` — i.e. it really *is* inside `0..=31`. It was correct. But it's phrased as a claim rather than a diagnosis, which is exactly how it misread, so I changed it to "GET_RAMDISK must stay clear of the 0..=31 MINIX-mirrored block" and noted why in a comment.

**5. Emitting `GET_RAMDISK` in the C headers — declined, and recorded as a decision.** `GET_WHOAMI` is emitted and describes any process; `GET_RAMDISK` is kernel-gated to `MEM_PROC_NR`, a Rust driver, so no C can call it successfully. Past the D8 freeze a header constant costs a two-repo PR to retract. Rather than leave the asymmetry looking accidental, I added `no_ramdisk_selector_is_emitted_yet` — the repo's existing `no_grant_struct_is_emitted_yet` pattern — which asserts `GET_WHOAMI` *is* emitted and the ramdisk selector is not, with the reason and a note to delete the test when a C caller appears.

**Verification after the changes:** `fmt --check`, `clippy --workspace --all-targets`, both kernel clippy configs clean; 392 host tests pass (gen-c-headers 56 → 57); C-header gate compiles and writes nothing into the tree; boot passes all 72 markers. No `MUTATION` residue outside the CLAUDE.md line that documents the procedure.

Still uncommitted, as you asked.

cd /Users/kevinbarnard/src/minixrs
git commit -F - <<'MSG'
slice 5.7: BDEV band + `memory` ramdisk driver + `tools/mkfs-mfs` + rootfs blob

Builds the bottom two layers of the storage stack Phase 5's milestone needs
(D3): a MinixFS v3 image built at compile time, packed into the MXBI archive as
a non-ELF blob, copied into RAM frames and mapped into the `memory` driver's
address space at boot, and served over a new BDEV request band. Slice 5.8 puts
MFS on top of it; 5.9 closes the milestone.

ABI. `BDEV_RQ_BASE = 0xA00`, between VFS (`0x800`) and CDEV (`0xB00`), leaving
`0x900` for 5.8's VFS<->FS band — four in-tree comments recorded that pairing
the other way round and are corrected here; only ascending order is
load-bearing. Payload mirrors CDEV: `{minor, grant, len, block}`, with **no
granter field** (the driver takes it from the kernel-stamped `m_source`, the
5.2/5.3 confused-deputy rule) and **no grant-offset field** (every client
through 5.9 grants a buffer whose block starts at 0). Reply `m_type` is the
byte count.

Two deliberate departures from CDEV. An over-long or out-of-range request is
`EINVAL`, not a short read: a short *write* is a POSIX contract clients loop
over, but a filesystem cannot interpret half a block, and `EIO` stays reserved
for Phase 6's real media errors. And `BDEV_WRITE` is defined now and answers
`EROFS`, not `ENOSYS` — `ENOSYS` is already the unknown-`m_type` answer, so
reusing it would make "doesn't know about writes" and "knows and refuses"
indistinguishable. It validates before refusing, so 5.10 replaces one line.

Kernel. `uspace::RAMDISK_WINDOW_BASE = 0x8000_0000` (one L1 slot, 4 MiB) sits
*above* the device window on purpose: `region::REGION_LIMIT` is the base of the
lowest kernel-owned window, so VM needs no edit when a window is added. The
pre-map is a `nr == MEM_PROC_NR` arm in `load_boot_server` beside TTY's — not in
`load_exec_image`, which `do_exec` shares — with no TLB or cache maintenance
(both justified in situ) and no `prot.device` involvement, since these are
ordinary RAM frames. Every step `.expect()`s: a non-advancing loop must panic on
`AlreadyMapped`, not leave a 1-page ramdisk and 255 leaked frames. New
`SYS_GETINFO` selector `GET_RAMDISK = 64` returns `(va, len)`, gated on the
caller being the `memory` driver. `pack_mxbi` gained u32 guards on its record
offsets, lengths, and total size.

Driver. `drivers/memory` has no `unsafe` block and never dereferences its
mapping: client transfers go through `SYS_SAFECOPY` and the boot self-check
through `SYS_COPY(SELF -> SELF)`, so an unmapped page is an `EFAULT` return
rather than an EL0 abort. Its check is device-level, not format-level — it reads
a 32-byte image header from block 0's boot block, never a superblock — so
Phase 6 can drop virtio-blk in under an unchanged MFS.

Three amendments to the written scope, each forced by a repo lesson:

  * The image is a **fixed** 256 blocks (1 MiB), not content-sized. The
    musl-sysroot-absent fallback packs a 15 KB `worker` ELF as `hello`, so a
    content-sized image would make every size-derived marker config-dependent —
    the 5.5/5.6 trap. Oversizing is a build failure naming one constant.
  * `/etc/pattern` (40 KiB) is mandatory, not filler: the real `hello` is ~200 KB
    and forces the single-indirect zone arm, but the fallback one fits inside the
    seven direct zones, so that arm and mkfs's indirect writer would be dead in
    exactly the config CI's non-QEMU jobs build.
  * MEM verifies an image header plus a tail label rather than a superblock. The
    tail is not decoration: a copy loop that failed to advance maps 256 pages of
    block 0 and passes every header check.

The image-header ABI lives in `kernel-shared::rootfs` rather than in mkfs, because
mkfs writes those bytes and MEM and VFS read them, and none of the three may
depend on the others — the `com::ROOTFS_MODULE_NAME` reason.

VFS gains a live client, run last in `main`'s prologue so a hang localizes to
`bdev.*` instead of blacking out 5.2/5.3/5.4's markers. It exists because there
is no successful `SAFECOPY_TO` anywhere else in the tree: `BDEV_READ` is the
first copy that writes into a grantee's buffer and succeeds, so without it the
kernel's `CPF_WRITE` + `Prot::writable` success path stays unproven until 5.8.

Verified: fmt, `clippy --workspace --all-targets`, both kernel clippy configs,
392 host tests, the C-header gate, and three boots — default,
`--no-default-features`, and musl-sysroot-absent — carrying every 5.7 marker
identically. Seven mutations confirmed each marker moves for its own reason.

gh pr create --base main --head feature/slice-5.7-bdev-ramdisk \
  --title "slice 5.7: BDEV band + \`memory\` ramdisk driver + \`tools/mkfs-mfs\` + rootfs blob" \
  --body-file - <<'BODY'
Builds the bottom two layers of the storage stack Phase 5's milestone needs (decision **D3**): a MinixFS v3 image built at compile time, packed into the MXBI archive as a non-ELF blob, copied into RAM frames and mapped into the `memory` driver's address space at boot, and served over a new **BDEV** request band. Slice 5.8 puts MFS on top of it; 5.9 closes the milestone.

Nothing here is speculative infrastructure: MFS (5.8) needs a block device, and the `memory` ramdisk is the shape MINIX 3 itself boots with — Phase 6 swaps virtio-blk in under an unchanged MFS.

## ABI

`BDEV_RQ_BASE = 0xA00`, between VFS (`0x800`) and CDEV (`0xB00`), leaving `0x900` for 5.8's VFS↔FS band. Four in-tree comments recorded that pairing the other way round and are corrected here; only *ascending order* is load-bearing, which is what made the correction free.

Payload mirrors CDEV — `{minor, grant, len, block}` — with **no granter field** (the driver takes it from the kernel-stamped `m_source`, the 5.2/5.3 confused-deputy rule) and **no grant-offset field** (every client through 5.9 grants a buffer whose block starts at 0). Reply `m_type` **is** the byte count.

Two deliberate departures from CDEV, each with its own doc comment:

- **An over-long or out-of-range request is `EINVAL`, not a short read.** A short *write* is a POSIX contract every client already loops over; a short *block read* is useless, because a filesystem cannot interpret half a block. `EIO` stays reserved for Phase 6's real media errors, where the request was well-formed and the *device* failed.
- **`BDEV_WRITE` is defined now and answers `EROFS`**, not `ENOSYS`. `ENOSYS` is already the unknown-`m_type` answer, so reusing it would make "doesn't know about writes" and "knows and refuses" indistinguishable. It validates *before* refusing, so slice 5.10 replaces one line rather than adding a validator.

## Kernel

`uspace::RAMDISK_WINDOW_BASE = 0x8000_0000` (one L1 slot, 4 MiB) sits **above** the device window on purpose: `region::REGION_LIMIT` is the base of the *lowest* kernel-owned window, so VM needs no edit when a window is added — and a `const _` assert keeps that ordering true.

The pre-map is a `nr == MEM_PROC_NR` arm in `load_boot_server` beside TTY's, deliberately **not** in `load_exec_image` (shared with `do_exec`, so every exec'd binary would inherit a ramdisk). No TLB maintenance (TTY's two reasons), no cache maintenance (kernel and driver both go through Normal-WB mappings, and it is data), and no `prot.device` involvement — these are ordinary RAM frames taking the normal `free_frame` path in all five leaf sweeps.

Every step `.expect()`s. A `let _ = map_page_in(..)` would turn a non-advancing loop into a 1-page ramdisk with 255 leaked frames instead of an `AlreadyMapped` panic.

New `SYS_GETINFO` selector `GET_RAMDISK = 64` returns `(va, len)`, gated on the caller being the `memory` driver — the ramdisk is mapped into exactly one address space, so the VA is actively misleading anywhere else. No new kernel call and no new kernel statics. `pack_mxbi` gained u32 guards on record offsets, lengths, and the archive's total size.

## Driver

`drivers/memory` contains **no `unsafe` block** and never dereferences its mapping: client transfers go through `SYS_SAFECOPY`, and even the boot self-check goes through `SYS_COPY(SELF → SELF)`. So a page the kernel failed to map surfaces as an `EFAULT` return value rather than an EL0 data abort — a better diagnostic than TTY's — and there is no MMIO sibling module and no new Sonar exclusion.

Its self-check is **device-level, not format-level**: it reads a 32-byte image header from block 0's boot block (bytes `0..1024`, which MinixFS never reads), never a superblock. A block driver that decoded a superblock would depend on the filesystem format, which is precisely the dependency Phase 6 has to unwind.

## Three amendments to the written scope

Each is forced by a lesson already in the tree:

1. **The image is a fixed 256 blocks (1 MiB), not content-sized.** In the musl-sysroot-absent fallback `build_hello` returns the 15 KB `worker` ELF, so a content-sized image would make every size-derived marker config-dependent — the 5.5/5.6 "right in one config, vacuous in the other" trap. Oversizing is a *build* failure naming one constant.
2. **`/etc/pattern` (40 KiB) is mandatory, not filler.** `/bin/hello` is ~200 KB = 49 blocks and forces the single-indirect zone arm, but the fallback `hello` is 4 blocks — inside the seven direct zones — so that arm and mkfs's indirect writer would be dead in exactly the config CI's non-QEMU jobs build.
3. **MEM verifies an image header plus a tail label, not a superblock.** The tail is not decoration: a copy loop that failed to advance maps 256 pages of block 0 and passes every header check. Mutation-tested — sourcing every page from block 0 moved exactly one marker, `ramdisk FAIL tail label`.

One placement decision worth flagging for review: the image-header ABI lives in **`kernel-shared::rootfs`**, not in `tools/mkfs-mfs`. mkfs writes those bytes and MEM and VFS read them, and none of the three may depend on the others — the same resolution `com::ROOTFS_MODULE_NAME` already uses. `image.rs` re-exports them so the writer's constants still read locally.

## Why VFS gains a live client

The plan deferred BDEV IPC to 5.8, but **there is no successful `SAFECOPY_TO` anywhere in the tree today** — its only live uses are PM's two denial probes expecting `EPERM`/`EFAULT`. `BDEV_READ` is the first copy that writes into a grantee's buffer *and succeeds*, so without a client here the kernel's `CPF_WRITE` + `Prot::writable` success path stays unproven until 5.8, which would then be debugging a new protocol, a new server, and a never-exercised copy direction at once. The anti-spoof rule also cannot be host-tested (it is a property of an *absent* field), and `EROFS`-vs-`ENOSYS` is a comment until something observes the difference.

The demo runs **last** in `main`'s prologue so a hang localizes to `bdev.*` instead of blacking out 5.2/5.3/5.4's markers.

## New boot markers

```
[as] memory nr=3 ttbr0_pa=
[ramdisk] mem va=0x80000000 len=1048576 pages=256
[diag memory] sef ready
[diag memory] ramdisk ok blocks=256 tail=1
[diag vfs] bdev.ds ok ep=
[diag vfs] bdev.read ok n=32
[diag vfs] bdev.head ok match=1
[diag vfs] bdev.tail ok match=1
[diag vfs] bdev.deny ok n=10
```

Every one is identical with and without `boot-stubs` **and** with and without the musl sysroot — that is what the fixed image size buys. `blocks=256` cross-checks the header's own field against `GET_RAMDISK`'s length; head and tail do not subsume each other (a driver ignoring `block` returns the header for both); the ten refusals include the one grant check slice 5.3 could not reach — a `CPF_READ`-only grant used as a copy *destination*.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all --check`; `clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`; `clippy -p minixrs-kernel --target aarch64-unknown-none` in both feature configs — all clean.
- 392 host tests pass, including 22 mkfs round-trip tests that read a real image back through the same decoders slice 5.8's server will use.
- The C-header gate regenerates and compiles, writing nothing into the tree.
- Three boots — default, `--no-default-features`, and musl-sysroot-absent — all carry every 5.7 marker; `check-boot-log.sh` passes all 72 on the default config. The stub-free run's only misses are the four pre-existing stub markers.
- **Seven mutations**, each restored and `diff -q`'d clean: drop the `memory` row (all `bdev.*` *and* 5.4's init markers vanish — why the demo runs last); source every page from block 0 (`ramdisk FAIL tail label`); reply `OK` instead of the count; pack `memory` after `vfs`; delete the `GET_RAMDISK` gate; route `BDEV_WRITE` into the `_` arm (`rc=-38`); revert `BDEV_WRITE` to a bare `EROFS` (`rc=-30`).

One honest negative result: **the reordering mutation did not move its marker.** Packing `memory` after `vfs` left `bdev.ds ok` intact — the DS publish still won the race. That is a finding about the property rather than the marker: publish-before-retrieve genuinely is luck, which is why the fallback exists. The `bdev.ds FAIL rc=-3 fallback=3` observation came from the drop-the-server mutation instead, and the lesson is recorded in CLAUDE.md.

**PR #48 is open with all thirteen checks green.**

https://github.com/minixrs/minixrs/pull/48

Commit `f8d313b` — 42 files, +4987/−112 — GPG-signed and verified by GitHub (`{"reason":"valid","verified":true}`).

Every gate passed, including the three that matter most for this slice:

- **QEMU boot smoke** (1m50s) — CI booted the real kernel with the recursive submodule checkout and `tools/build-musl.sh`, so it exercised the *real* `hello` path, not the fallback, and all 72 markers matched.
- **generated C headers** — the new BDEV band renders and the re-chained `_Static_assert`s compile under the hermetic `-nostdlibinc` check.
- **cargo-deny / cargo-audit** — the two new crates add only path dependencies, so the allow-list is undisturbed.

`miri` and `geiger` (both advisory) also passed with the three new packages added to the miri list.

One note for whoever reviews: the substantive judgement call to check is the placement of the image-header ABI in `kernel-shared::rootfs` rather than `tools/mkfs-mfs`. The plan put those constants in mkfs, but also forbade MEM and VFS from depending on `minixrs-mfs` — and both need to read the header, so as written the plan had no home for them. I called it out explicitly in the PR body rather than burying it.
